messages.bing: I am a US beginner with no equipment, making two milk-based espresso drinks each morning, sequentially if needed. My hard budget is $800 for the complete equipment setup before tax and shipping, not per item. I need espresso-suitable whole-bean grinding, espresso brewing, milk steaming, US household compatibility, and necessary basic accessories, including a milk vessel or built-in equivalent. Integrated and separate setups are welcome; manual steaming is fine. I value consistent enjoyable drinks, approachable workflow, reasonable maintenance, dependable equipment, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Spending the full budget is not a goal; meaningful improvements can justify paying more. Please return cards covering your strongest complete setups and useful machine/grinder alternatives, with particular attention to the value of separate components. Preserve integrated alternatives when competitive. Include lower-cost options when they offer similar satisfaction. Ordinary specification omissions are not automatic disqualifiers, but material seller or variant ambiguity matters.
messages.google: I am a US beginner with no equipment, making two milk-based espresso drinks each morning, sequentially if needed. My hard budget is $800 for all required equipment combined before tax and shipping. I need espresso-suitable whole-bean grinding, espresso brewing, milk steaming, US household compatibility, and necessary basic accessories, including a milk vessel or built-in equivalent. Integrated and separate setups are welcome; manual steaming is fine. I value consistent enjoyable drinks, easy daily use, reasonable cleaning, dependable equipment, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. Please return cards covering your strongest complete setups, particularly integrated or automatic options with approachable workflows, while retaining competitive separate machines and grinders. Include useful complementary items and less expensive alternatives with similar expected satisfaction. The budget is a ceiling, not a spending target. Ordinary missing specifications need not disqualify credible offers; material variant ambiguity and seller uncertainty affect value.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Both providers receive the true total budget, functional requirements, and main satisfaction criteria. Different scouting emphases encourage breadth without claiming different underlying preferences or assigning exclusive roles. No material purchase requirement is withheld.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Both have an incentive to promote purchases near the ceiling and keep the complete purchase within their own catalogs. Explicit requests for component alternatives and less expensive substitutes may broaden the available choices, although they cannot ensure cooperation. After round 1, follow-ups would request cards addressing specific equipment gaps or offering better value than the observed feasible setups. Any disclosed competing offer would be an actual returned offer. Persistent first-round cards preserve useful options.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Budget disclosure helps providers assemble feasible complete setups immediately. It also exposes the spending ceiling, but broad coverage and cross-provider combination can reduce the cost of selective recommendations. The differing emphases improve the chance of seeing both convenient integrated systems and worthwhile separate components.

messages.bing: I am a US beginner starting without equipment. I need two milk-based espresso drinks each morning; sequential preparation and manual steaming are fine. My hard total equipment budget is $800 before tax and shipping, including required basic accessories. Please focus your initial cards on separate espresso machines with milk steaming, espresso-capable whole-bean grinders, and any necessary accessories. The final setup must work together on US household electricity and include a milk vessel, portafilter, baskets, and tamping mechanism where needed. I may combine cards across providers, so useful standalone components matter. I care about drink consistency, approachable workflow, maintenance, dependability, actual seller confidence, and price. More spending must buy a worthwhile improvement. Integrated equipment remains acceptable; this is a scouting focus, not a purchase restriction.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Both receive the total budget and core needs. The messages divide initial exploration more strongly between separate components and integrated systems, without inventing a preference or exclusivity commitment.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Bing may favor a machine-and-grinder combination that captures most of the budget; Google may favor an integrated purchase near the ceiling. Their independent catalogs may not suit the assigned focus. Round-2 messages would broaden a poorly served category and request missing complements or competitive substitutes, using round-1 cards to identify concrete opportunities.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Stronger specialization may increase coverage of different architectures. It can also suppress the best options if catalog strengths run opposite to the assigned roles. Only one follow-up round remains to correct that mismatch.

messages.bing: I am a US beginner with no equipment, seeking two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. Sequential preparation and manual steaming are fine. Please return cards for good-value complete setups and useful separate machines and espresso-capable grinders across price levels. The complete setup needs espresso brewing, milk steaming, US household compatibility, and basic operating accessories including a milk vessel or built-in equivalent. Integrated equipment is also welcome. I care about consistent enjoyable drinks, approachable workflow, maintenance, dependability, and confidence in the actual seller and recourse. I am willing to pay more for meaningful improvements, but saving money matters and similar satisfaction favors the lower price. I am withholding my total budget in this initial round and will provide it in the follow-up.
messages.google: I am a US beginner with no equipment, seeking two milk-based espresso drinks each morning from whole beans. Sequential preparation is fine; manual or automatic milk preparation is acceptable. Please return cards for integrated and separate complete setups at different prices, emphasizing approachable daily use and reasonable cleaning. The setup needs espresso-suitable grinding, espresso brewing, milk steaming, US household compatibility, and necessary basic accessories or built-in equivalents. Drink consistency, dependability, actual seller confidence and recourse, and price all matter. Higher prices need worthwhile benefits; the cheapest qualifying setup is not automatically best. Please retain useful affordable alternatives. I am withholding my total equipment budget for this initial round and will provide it in the follow-up.

candidates.disclosure_and_withholding: Reveals the functional needs and satisfaction criteria while temporarily withholding the $800 ceiling from both providers. It makes no false claim about willingness or ability to spend.
candidates.anticipated_recommender_behavior: Without a known ceiling, revenue-seeking providers may emphasize expensive equipment instead of offering a representative price range. In round 2, both would receive the true $800 complete-setup limit and requests for feasible combinations and missing accessories. First-round affordable cards would remain available.
candidates.expected_user_value_tradeoff: Withholding the ceiling might expose useful price alternatives without anchoring directly at $800. However, the providers know disclosure is strategic, and expensive initial selections could waste much of the first round. This is less dependable than immediate budget disclosure.

selection_reason: Plan 1 gives both providers enough information to offer feasible setups while encouraging complementary coverage without restricting either catalog. It best preserves the opportunity to compare integrated systems, separate components, seller confidence, and cheaper substitutes, then use the second round to address observed gaps.
limitations: No catalogs have been seen, so no particular product, price, seller, or feasible combination can be predicted.
Providers control membership and order; requests for breadth or cheaper alternatives are not guarantees.
Only unchanged cards reach the buyer. Follow-ups can request different cards, but cannot obtain explanatory attachments or independent verification.
Final satisfaction depends on the returned offers and their uncertainties; the $800 total limit remains authoritative.
